newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia tests engine for Lockheed rocket.
newsitem.headline: Russia tests engine for Lockheed rocket.

text.p: Russian rocket engine maker NPO Energomash has carried out the first test of its new RD-180 engine, selected by Lockheed Martin Astronautics to power its Atlas IIAR rocket, a company spokesman said on Thursday.
The rocket is due to enter service in 1998.

The Energomash spokesman quoted the company's chief designer Boris Katorgin as saying after the test, carried out over two days last week: "We have got very important results and we have demonstrated...our cooperation".
He said a Lockheed Martin Astronautics official attended the test and that "he was extremely pleased with the result".
Energomash has been working on the RD-180 together with Pratt and Whitney, a division of United Technologies Corp. Their partnership began in 1992.

Their 20 year cooperation programme involves developing, producing, testing, certifing and marketing the RD-180 which was derived from the proven RD-170 engine, the company official said, adding that it would be one of the world's most powerful liquid-fuelled rocket engines.
This April, Russia approved a deal to export RD-180 engines to the United States and later produce them there for government payloads.
RD-180s produced in Russia will be used only for commercial launches in the United States. Moscow has banned their use by the U.S. government, fearing it might launch spy satellites with them.
